code: #include <RcppEnsmallen.h> // [[Rcpp::depends(RcppEnsmallen)]] // Define a constrained objective function. On top of the Evaluate() and // Gradient() pair that a differentiable function supplies, the constrained // contract adds NumConstraints(), EvaluateConstraint() and // GradientConstraint(). class NonNegativeLeastSquaresFunction { public:     // Construct the object with the given design matrix and responses.     NonNegativeLeastSquaresFunction(const arma::mat& X, const arma::vec& y) :     X(X), y(y) { }      // Return the residual sum of squares for coefficients beta.     double Evaluate(const arma::mat& beta)     {         const arma::vec r = y - X * beta;         return arma::dot(r, r);     }      // Compute the gradient of the residual sum of squares.     void Gradient(const arma::mat& beta, arma::mat& g)     {         g = -2.0 * X.t() * (y - X * beta);     }      // One constraint per coefficient, each one a lower bound of zero.     size_t NumConstraints() const { return X.n_cols; }      // Return the residual of constraint i, which is zero when beta_i is     // non-negative and equal to beta_i when it is not.     //     // ensmallen only ever passes an index below NumConstraints(). The bounds     // test guards against a caller that reuses this class directly, since     // beta(i, 0) is unchecked once NDEBUG is set.     double EvaluateConstraint(const size_t i, const arma::mat& beta)     {         if (i >= X.n_cols) return 0.0;          return std::min(0.0, beta(i, 0));     }      // Compute the gradient of constraint i, the derivative of the clamped     // residual returned above.     void GradientConstraint(const size_t i, const arma::mat& beta,                             arma::mat& g)     {         g.zeros(beta.n_rows, beta.n_cols);          if (i < X.n_cols && beta(i, 0) < 0.0) g(i, 0) = 1.0;     }  private:     // The design matrix.     const arma::mat& X;     // The responses to each data point.     const arma::vec& y; }; // [[Rcpp::export]] arma::vec nnls_auglag(const arma::mat& X, const arma::vec& y) {      // Construct the objective function.     NonNegativeLeastSquaresFunction nnls(X, y);      // Create the augmented Lagrangian optimizer with default parameters. It     // solves a sequence of unconstrained problems with L-BFGS, raising the     // penalty on violated constraints between rounds.     ens::AugLagrangian auglag;      // A vector of zeros is feasible, so optimization begins inside the     // feasible region and the result is reproducible.     arma::mat beta(X.n_cols, 1, arma::fill::zeros);      // Run the optimization.     auglag.Optimize(nnls, beta);      return beta; }

code: #include <RcppEnsmallen.h> // [[Rcpp::depends(RcppEnsmallen)]] class LogisticRegressionFunction { public:     // Construct the object with the given design matrix, responses, and     // ridge penalty.     LogisticRegressionFunction(const arma::mat& X,                                const arma::vec& y,                                const double lambda) :     X(X), y(y), lambda(lambda) { }      // Return the objective function for model parameters beta.     // ensmallen passes beta as a p x 1 matrix, one entry per column of X.     double Evaluate(const arma::mat& beta)     {         // The n x 1 linear predictor.         const arma::vec eta = X * beta;         // One number: the loss summed over rows, plus the ridge penalty. Its         // 0.5 is what makes the penalty differentiate to lambda * beta below.         return arma::accu(softplus(eta) - y % eta) +             0.5 * lambda * arma::accu(arma::square(beta));     }      // Compute the gradient for model parameters beta.     void Gradient(const arma::mat& beta, arma::mat& g)     {         const arma::vec eta = X * beta;         // Nothing is returned; the p x 1 gradient is written into g.         g = X.t() * (logistic(eta) - y) + lambda * beta;     }  private:     // The design matrix, held by const reference so no copy is made.     const arma::mat& X;     // The responses to each data point.     const arma::vec& y;     // The ridge penalty applied to every coefficient.     const double lambda; }; // Compute both at once, reusing the single pass over eta.     double EvaluateWithGradient(const arma::mat& beta, arma::mat& g)     {         const arma::vec eta = X * beta;         g = X.t() * (logistic(eta) - y) + lambda * beta;         return arma::accu(softplus(eta) - y % eta) +             0.5 * lambda * arma::accu(arma::square(beta));     } // [[Rcpp::export]] arma::vec logistic_reg_lbfgs(const arma::mat& X, const arma::vec& y,                              const double lambda = 0.0) {      // Construct the objective function.     LogisticRegressionFunction lrf(X, y, lambda);      // Create the L-BFGS optimizer with default parameters. The ens::L_BFGS     // type can be replaced with any ensmallen optimizer that can handle     // differentiable functions.     ens::L_BFGS lbfgs;      // The objective is convex, so a deterministic start of zeros reaches the     // same optimum a random start would.     arma::mat beta(X.n_cols, 1, arma::fill::zeros);      // Run the optimization.     lbfgs.Optimize(lrf, beta);      return beta; }

code: // The same objective in separable form, which is what the mini-batch // optimizers require: ensmallen hands it one batch of rows at a time. // There is no lambda here, so this is the unpenalized negative log-likelihood. class LogisticRegressionSeparableFunction { public:     // Construct the object, copying the design matrix and responses.     LogisticRegressionSeparableFunction(const arma::mat& X,                                         const arma::vec& y) :     X(X), y(y) { }      // Return the number of separable functions, one per observation.     size_t NumFunctions() const { return X.n_rows; }      // Shuffle the order of the observations.     void Shuffle()     {         const arma::uvec ordering =             arma::shuffle(arma::regspace<arma::uvec>(0, X.n_rows - 1));         X = X.rows(ordering);         y = y.elem(ordering);     }      // Return the objective summed over the batch [begin, begin + batchSize).     // Note this is a sum, not a mean; ensmallen expects the former.     double Evaluate(const arma::mat& beta,                     const size_t begin,                     const size_t batchSize)     {         // begin and batchSize index rows of X, so last is the final row used.         const size_t last = begin + batchSize - 1;         // batchSize x 1 here, where the full-batch class had n x 1.         const arma::vec eta = X.rows(begin, last) * beta;         const arma::vec yBatch = y.subvec(begin, last);          return arma::accu(softplus(eta) - yBatch % eta);     }      // Compute the gradient over the batch [begin, begin + batchSize).     void Gradient(const arma::mat& beta,                   const size_t begin,                   arma::mat& g,                   const size_t batchSize)     {         const size_t last = begin + batchSize - 1;
